+orchestration groups the run header, model recommendation, policy decision,
+resolved candidate, evidence, operator choices, progress, and final summary.

+file and network permissions. Notes wrap their contents; phase updates use
+static notes, avoiding Clack's native spinner and its input/signal ownership.
+
+`--plain`, non-TTY input/output, CI, `NO_COLOR`, and `TERM=dumb` select static
+output. Plain input explicitly disables readline's terminal rendering so it
+does not emit cursor controls even inside a TTY. Decision-only output remains

+review and separate approval; task acceptance still requires completion

+# Offline terminal verification
+
+This optional harness drives the compiled or installed CLI in a real POSIX PTY
+or Windows ConPTY. It does not call live models or coding agents. Its native
+test dependencies have a separate manifest and lockfile; ordinary development
+and the published package do not install them.
+
+```bash
+pnpm --dir scripts/terminal install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm verify:terminal --output /absolute/new/evidence-directory
+```
+
+Use a new output directory outside the repository. On Windows, supply an
+absolute Windows path, for example `C:/Temp/dev-ui-check`. The directory retains
+fixtures, traces, application bytes, PTY bytes, reconstructed screens, and a
+JSON report even after failure. Each scenario has a 30-second deadline and a
+2 MiB output bound. `--only styled-40` selects one scenario for diagnosis.
+
+To check an independently installed checkout archive, use:
+
+```bash
+pnpm verify:terminal --cli /absolute/consumer/node_modules/dev-orchestrator/dist/cli.js --output /absolute/new/packed-evidence
+```
+
+The CLI path is resolved through package-manager symlinks. The
+[terminal CI workflow](../../.github/workflows/terminal.yml) builds, packs,
+installs a private consumer, and runs both variants on Ubuntu and Windows with
+Node 22. Its artifacts retain both reports and captures for seven days. It
+does not publish an npm package.
+
+## Boundaries and assertions
+
+The harness starts disposable Git repositories with long paths, spaces, and
+Unicode. It intercepts only the fixed TypeSafe endpoint and the worker/check
+process boundaries. Requested Codex, Claude, and `npm run test` processes
+become local Node fixtures. Read-only Git inspection, the real process runner,
+policy, candidate selection, approvals, independent check transitions, and
+trace writing remain real. Child environments contain a small OS allowlist
+and a synthetic credential. Production credentials and local value files are
+not loaded. Timeout cases shorten the existing 15-minute timer to 150 ms at
+the test clock boundary; this does not change the production deadline.
+
+The 33 scenarios per platform cover 40/60/80/120 columns, both adapters,
+explicit networking, plain/non-TTY/CI/`NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb`, repair, recovery,
+invalid input, budgets, prompt EOF/timeout/signals, alternative confirmation,
+active execution and evaluation cancellation, and typed stop/quit. POSIX tests
+include active SIGTERM and a TERM-resistant descendant. Windows substitutes an
+extra plain Ctrl+D/Enter case; plain Ctrl+Z/Enter is also checked. Both modes
+preserve separate completion acceptance and fresh independent checks.
+
+`@xterm/headless` reconstructs the screen, including cursor movement and
+wrapping. Checks compare the candidate parameters retained by the trace with
+the rendered review, with trace depth truncation treated as unavailable data.
+Initial worker and validation parameters are compared in full. Application
+output is captured before ConPTY encoding: ConPTY itself can emit VT frames
+even when the application is completely plain. Additional checks cover signal
+listeners, raw input/cursor restoration, POSIX terminal flags, partial edits,
+process exit, validation generations, budgets, credential redaction, terminal
+injection, schema-v2 traces, and schema-v1 JSON/traces with and without
+`--plain`.
+
+The driver pins [node-pty 1.1.0](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty/tree/v1.1.0)
+and [xterm headless 6.0.0](https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/tree/6.0.0).
+Only node-pty's exact build is allowed in this isolated pnpm workspace; Linux
+needs Python, make, and a C++ compiler. Windows uses its packaged native
+bindings and bundled ConPTY. An isolated, asserted cleanup shim disposes the
+driver's retained ConPTY worker after the CLI has exited, avoiding the
+[upstream natural-exit leak](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty/issues/965).
+Review that shim when upgrading the pinned driver. It is absent from the
+production CLI and does not establish application cleanup on its behalf.
+
+These checks establish terminal presentation and enforcement with synthetic
+boundaries. They do not establish live model quality, native worker/package
+manager launcher availability, screen-reader certification, or GUI font
+appearance.

+## Presentation and enforcement
+
+The matrix covers 33 scenarios per platform. Reviews at 40, 60, 80, and 120
+columns preserve initial worker and validation parameters in full, including
+absolute paths, spaces, Unicode, quoted task text, and permission settings.
+Later nested context is compared against the fields retained by bounded
+traces; a trace truncation marker is not treated as an original value.
+Fixture repository paths span roughly 148–173 characters, rather than testing
+filesystem maximum path lengths.
+
+Plain TTYs, pipes, CI, `NO_COLOR`, and `TERM=dumb` produce no application ANSI
+output. Static reviews retain named sections, complete parameters, text status
+labels, typed choices, limits, and final validation evidence. This text review
+does not rely on color, animation, or a highlighted default. Headless terminal
+reconstruction checks actual wrapping and cursor movement; it is not a GUI
+font or screen-reader certification.
+
+The real policy and approval loop retain explicit recovery, separately
+confirmed alternatives, completion acceptance after fresh independent checks,
+current-generation repair, immutable worker/network selection, and existing
+budgets. Both adapters and explicit Codex networking are exercised. Invalid
+input approves nothing, and eight rejections exhaust the iteration budget
+without a worker call.
+
+EOF, timeout, and signals are exercised at approval, clarification, and
+recovery prompts. Escape and EOF during resolved completion approval stop
+without inventing approval or acceptance. Active evaluation and worker
+interruption retain conventional exits and bounded evidence. POSIX execution
+also checks a TERM-resistant descendant and SIGTERM; Windows checks direct
+child cancellation through Ctrl+C. Partial edits remain, validation is not
+claimed, and fixture worker processes are checked dead before driver cleanup.
+
+POSIX terminal flags, both platforms' raw-mode and cursor restoration, and
+owned signal-listener cleanup are asserted. Application bytes are captured
+before ConPTY's own VT encoding, so transport frames cannot be mistaken for
+application styling. JSON and traces retain their existing schemas and contain
+no renderer preferences, styling bytes, or configured synthetic credential.

+## Finding and fix
+
+Plain Windows console input delivered Ctrl+D/Ctrl+Z as a submitted control
+line instead of closing stdin. The initial checks waited for input and failed
+their deadline. The adapter now treats an otherwise empty EOF control line
+from a TTY as `input_closed`, latches the closed-input state, and stops with
+exit `1`. Plain mode remains line-oriented: Windows users press Enter after
+the control key. Styled Ctrl+D remains immediate. Two focused cases cover both
+keys, no raw-mode activation, no ANSI output, and rejection of later prompts.
+
+The harness also exposed its own setup issues: the PTY driver initially
+overrode `TERM=dumb`, screen comparison needed the displayed bidi escapes and
+bounded trace truncation, and node-pty retained its Windows conout worker after
+the CLI exited. These were corrected in verification tooling. Its pinned,
+asserted driver cleanup is separate from application cleanup and is never
+shipped. Earlier failing captures are retained.
+

+

+## Choice probability precision in POST /v1/systemone
+
+We are investigating [petercr/jev-orchestrator#61](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/issues/61), a publication blocker for our manually approved coding orchestrator. We call the TypeSafe endpoint directly with Node fetch; no TypeSafe or Vercel SDK processes the native response.

+Our 2026-10-22 live pilot recorded four rejected next-action distributions in 26 evaluations: totals of `0.99` or `0.9900000000000001`. Three explicit recoveries succeeded; a run stopped on its second invalid response after its implementation and independent checks had passed. We retain only allowlisted diagnostics for failed evaluations, so their underlying served model and full distributions are unavailable. Successful evaluations requested `jev-latest` and reported `jev-1.14.0`.
+
+The request asks four Noul questions plus one Choice over nine actions. The action criteria cover repository reads, tests, two coding workers, user clarification, and completion. The consumer validates finite probabilities in [0,1], exact action keys, selected-option consistency, and a total within 0.001 of 1. It never renormalizes probabilities or modifies reported confidence. The sum diagnostic is calculated directly from the response probabilities before any policy or tool execution.
+
+The current [OpenAPI schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) describes totals as approximately 1. We found no probability-precision setting in that request schema or in the official JavaScript SDK at `b844cd1aca12855a5d24a2df52a1401c86e7d37a`. All six passed, with wire probability values unchanged through our parser. This small probe did not reproduce the invalid total and does not establish pinning as a remedy. We are preserving the original failed observations.

+# Issue #61: distribution precision investigation
+
+[Issue #61](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/issues/61) remains open
+and blocks v0.5 publication. The investigation found a compatibility gap
+between the provider's approximate-total contract and this repository's strict
+sum requirement. It has not established a supported precision setting, a
+successful mitigation, or the provider's internal cause. No production
+behavior, tolerance, model default, or recovery limit has changed.
+
+## What the retained evidence establishes
+
+The [original pilot](v0.5-live-results.md) retains four `distribution/sum`
+rejections in 26 evaluations, with totals near 0.99. Those failures occurred
+on direct TypeSafe REST. The provider and SDK layers must be distinguished:
+
+- [evaluateNative](../../src/ai/native.ts) sends the request through `fetch`,
+  bounds the response, parses JSON with duplicate-key rejection, then calls
+  `normalizeAssessment`. No TypeSafe or Vercel SDK handles that route.
+- [normalizeAssessment](../../src/ai/contract.ts) checks action names and
+  finite values, copies each probability unchanged, adds the received values,
+  and rejects totals outside 0.001. It does not round or renormalize them.
+- The approximately 0.01 discrepancy is materially larger than ordinary
+  floating-point summation error for nine bounded numbers. The retained
+  diagnostic therefore identifies received values incompatible with our sum
+  requirement, rather than a display-only rounding of a valid total.
+- Full failed response bodies were deliberately not retained. Their exact
+  distributions, served-model identity, and the upstream implementation that
+  generated them remain unavailable. Quantization is a plausible explanation,
+  not a demonstrated provider-internal cause.
+
+The published [TypeSafe OpenAPI schema](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json)
+describes Choice probabilities as summing approximately to one. Its request
+properties are `model`, `state`, `questions`, and `assets`; it documents no
+probability-precision control. The official
+[JavaScript SDK source](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/tree/b844cd1aca12855a5d24a2df52a1401c86e7d37a/src)
+also exposes no dedicated precision option at the inspected revision.
+This does not establish that an undocumented server option exists or works.
+
+The current [models documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) recommends
+version pinning for repeatability. A pin cannot by itself guarantee compliance
+with a stronger probability-sum contract. The previous
+[v0.4 live pilot](../workflows/v0.4-live-results-v1.md) also recorded invalid
+totals while successful evaluations reported `jev-1.13.0`.
+
+## Separate bounded read-only probe
+
+Before calling the service, freeze a new six-evaluation protocol: two synthetic
+workflow snapshots (before and after an instruction read), each evaluated with
+`jev-latest`, `jev-1.14.0`, and `jev-1.13.0`. The snapshots are diagnostic data;
+no orchestration, tools, workers, or saved-run resume are involved. Each model
+selection is fixed for its evaluation. The cap is six evaluations and twelve
+HTTP attempts, retaining the existing per-evaluation deadline and transient
+retry policy. No original pilot observation is replaced.

+integration with a read-only observer that compares parsed wire probabilities
+to the integration's returned probabilities. The bounded response bytes are
+passed through unchanged; bodies and individual probabilities are not saved.
+Only successful attribution, an unchanged-values flag, or existing allowlisted
+failure diagnostics may be retained. A rejected sum would additionally be
+checked against the wire sum in memory.
+
+| Requested model | Before read | After read | Served model on successful evaluations |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `jev-latest` | normalized, unchanged | normalized, unchanged | `jev-1.14.0` |
+| `jev-1.14.0` | normalized, unchanged | normalized, unchanged | `jev-1.14.0` |
+| `jev-1.13.0` | normalized, unchanged | normalized, unchanged | `jev-1.13.0` |
+
+All six evaluations completed in six HTTP attempts. No worker or repository
+action ran, and no result was replaced. This small probe did not reproduce the
+invalid totals. It verifies unchanged parsing for these successful responses;

and changelog from `fix/61-explicit-routing-recovery`. Install the archive
into a fresh offline consumer with lifecycle scripts disabled. Record its
source commit, archive hash, all installed hashes, exact launcher and receipt

pilot, and six-evaluation probe unchanged.

The launcher never answers prompts. Review and approve each instruction read,
worker call, independent test/lint command, and resolved completion candidate.

# Issue #61: explicit recovery mitigation candidate

The candidate verifies bounded, explicitly approved recovery while keeping
malformed responses rejected. It does **not** fix TypeSafe's probability
output. All three newly recorded live runs completed; one natural rejection
required recovery. Operator acceptance of this release tradeoff is still
outstanding, so [#61](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/issues/61)
continues to block publication.

## Proposed release mitigation

Keep the 0.001 sum tolerance, unchanged probabilities and confidence, and no
automatic retries of malformed responses. In orchestration mode, the operator
can review a rejected total and explicitly request another evaluation within
the remaining eight iterations. Each failure consumes an iteration. Recovery
preserves edits, evidence, worker call budgets, the bound provider/model, and
worker/network permissions; it never approves the rejected action. Every
subsequent action and task acceptance still requires its own approval.

This recovery behavior already existed. The production change is clearer
recovery guidance, including that another evaluation may fail. README and
release notes now disclose the observed TypeSafe limitation and distinguish
orchestration recovery from decision-only errors. The first pilot's artificial
one-recovery study cap is absent from this new protocol; removing that study
cap does not change production behavior or demonstrate better router quality.

Residual risk: repeated invalid answers can exhaust a run before acceptance,
even with a correct patch and passing checks. Stopping preserves changes and
diagnostics, returns failure, and does not accept the task. A new invocation
starts a separate run with new approvals; traces cannot resume execution.
There is no automatic provider/model/worker switch or networking escalation.
An operator who requires the provider to always meet the strict contract
should keep publication blocked pending an upstream fix.

## Frozen candidate and collection

The [new protocol](v0.5-routing-mitigation-protocol.md) was frozen before the
three launches. Candidate source: `4b49a1030d6a52421849efe76e220ceadda744f7`.

and task strings from the [first pilot](v0.5-live-protocol.md).

pnpm 11.19.0. The actual packaged CLI called direct TypeSafe `jev-latest` and
real Codex 0.163.0 / Claude Code 2.1.308. Successful evaluations reported
`jev-1.14.0`; the rejected response has no retained served-model attribution.
Codex used the adapter's `gpt-5.6-terra` / high, workspace-write, network off,
and `never` approval setting. Claude used `sonnet` / medium with restricted
file tools and private rename MCP; the alias's underlying model is unknown.
Existing credentials were loaded by Varlock without reading or printing
local value files. No live provider or worker boundary was mocked.

## Results and receipts

| Run | Worker / presentation | Final iteration | Rejections / explicit recoveries | Action approvals / alternatives | Independent checks | Exit / result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| r01 | Codex / plain, 80 columns | 5 | 0 / 0 | 5 / 2 | test at 3; lint at 4 | 0 / approved completion |
| r02 | Claude / styled, 60 columns | 6 | 1 / 1 | 5 / 2 | test at 4; lint at 5 | 0 / approved completion |
| r03 | Claude / plain, 80 columns | 5 | 0 / 0 | 5 / 2 | test at 3; lint at 4 | 0 / approved completion |

All patches met the four original examples and permitted only `tags.mjs`
and new `tags.test.mjs` edits. Each run used one selected-worker call. Both
independent checks passed in generation 1 after that attempt, before separate
FINISH selection, resolved review, and acceptance approval. Ambiguous worker
routes required manual selection; completion probabilities remained below the
95% automatic threshold. They were not raised to enable completion.

In r02, iteration 1 returned `invalid_response` at `distribution/sum`, total
`0.99`. Its failure trace has null evaluation, policy, approval, and tool
fields. The styled 60-column prompt displayed the new guidance and seven
remaining iterations. Explicit `continue` preceded iteration 2's new
instruction-read proposal; that action received its own approval. No rejected
recommendation ran, and no original observation was replaced.

Totals: 16 evaluations, one rejection, one explicit recovery, 21 action-review
requests, 15 approvals, six manual alternatives, three worker calls, and six
passing independent checks. Failure/recovery trace rows are deduplicated by
iteration. All three CLI processes exited and restored their terminal flags.
The audit confirmed immutable selection and networking, eight-iteration and
two-call bounds, retained evidence, and current-generation receipts. No
protocol deviations were observed.

Recorded active time totals 76.434 seconds; action-approval and recovery waits
total 178.828 seconds. No token usage, cost, or speed comparison is inferred.

## Deterministic and installed checks

- All 44 focused presentation/recovery tests passed, followed by typecheck,
  all 1,409 tests across 41 files, build, and schema-only environment checks.
- New HTTP/process-boundary regressions force totals 0.99 and 1.01 after a

  Two explicit recoveries preserve edits, validation generation, call counts,

  prompt/environment mutation, and a separate final acceptance approval.
  Existing tests retain stopping, cancellation, malformed-response rejection,
  no silent invalid-response retry, and exhaustion coverage.
- Fresh offline installation passed 49 CLI checks and 18 mocked transport

## Limits and release decision

Only one natural rejection occurred in this new cohort. Repeated recovery
**was not exercised live here**; the consecutive-rejection path is verified
by the deterministic regressions. The [original mixed pilot](v0.5-live-results.md)
retains four rejections and a stopped run, and the earlier six-evaluation
probe remains separate. This small new cohort establishes neither a failure
rate nor improved routing reliability. It reruns tag parsing, not the staged
repair, linked issues, other live providers, native Windows workers, or real
active-worker interruption.

Evidence is retained outside Git under
`/home/peterc/.cache/dev-issue61-mitigation-20261022`: frozen inputs and hashes,
archive and fresh consumer, exact launcher, process and terminal records,

validation receipts, results, audits, and installed/terminal verification.
No rejected provider body or credential value is retained.

Accepting this mitigation means accepting occasional failed evaluations and
possible budget exhaustion as a documented v0.5 limitation while preserving
strict rejection and manual recovery. It is not acceptance of approximate
probability totals. Until the operator explicitly accepts that tradeoff,
keep #61 open and npm publication blocked. After acceptance and merge,
recheck the retained candidate against merged inputs before publication.

PR #64 is merged. The earlier draft gives v0.6 a clear focus: save a run, inspect it, and resume it later with the remaining budget.

I’ll build the plan around that workflow, with a live stop-and-resume pilot required before release. The first milestone will settle durable storage and attempt accounting, since a restart must never repeat an uncertain worker action or reset its limits.

The code confirms two important gaps: the loop starts at iteration one, and worker calls are counted after execution. Saving the current state alone would therefore be insufficient.

I’m splitting the work into six small PRs: storage contract, saving, history, resume, failure and platform coverage, then the live pilot and release. The scope will cover clean stops on the same machine and worktree; ambiguous crashes will remain inspectable but blocked.

@@
 ## v0.6 draft: saved runs and safe resume
 
-Drafted on 2026-10-17 at the operator's request to plan v0.6. Saved runs and
-safe resume are the proposed focus, building on v0.4's workflow behavior and
-v0.5's presentation work. This is a design proposal; implementation has not
-started and the published CLI has no resume command.
-
-The intended outcome is to stop an opted-in orchestration run, close the
-terminal, and later continue the same task without reconstructing its context
-or losing track of consumed limits. A local history view should explain what
-happened, what remains, and whether continuation is possible. An existing
-task's partial edits stay in its working tree.
-
-### User workflow and first-release boundary
-
-Provisional command shape, to be finalized with CLI compatibility tests:
+Originally drafted on 2026-10-17. Refined on 2026-10-22 after publication of
+v0.5.0 and merge of its publication record in
+[PR #64](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/pull/64). This is the
+proposed v0.6 scope, ready for review. Implementation has not started; the
+published CLI has none of the saved-run options below.
+
+**Release outcome:** an operator can stop an opted-in task, close the terminal,
+inspect its history, and continue it in a new CLI process without losing its
+approved context or resetting its limits. Partial edits stay in the worktree.
+Resuming requires fresh repository checks, validation, and action approvals.
+
+### Product scope
+
+| Priority | Deliverable | Observable result |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Required | Opt-in saved orchestration | The CLI prints a run ID, checkpoints progress, and explains whether the stopped run can continue. |
+| Required | Local history and detail | The operator can see the task, repository, status, consumed/remaining budgets, pending checks, and any resume blocker without credentials or network access. |
+| Required | Explicit continuation | A cleanly stopped run continues in a new process on the same machine and canonical Git worktree, starting at its next unused iteration. |
+| Required | Conservative failure handling | Storage errors, unresolved execution, incompatible records, and concurrent ownership stop execution with a specific explanation. |
+| Required | Verified release | Offline restart/failure coverage, installed-package terminal checks, and a recorded live stop/resume pilot pass before publication. |
+
+Keep this release focused. Cross-machine transfer, crash recovery for uncertain
+execution, background runs, worker-native conversation restoration, automatic
+retries/failover, expanded permissions/budgets, a dashboard, and new providers
+are outside v0.6. Run deletion, export/import, and automatic retention cleanup
+are also deferred; the first version documents storage and manual housekeeping
+for inactive records. Existing runs without saving remain supported.
+
+The [v0.5 routing limitation](docs/presentation/v0.5-routing-mitigation-results.md)
+remains visible: invalid distributions are rejected at the same `0.001`
+tolerance, and explicit recovery consumes the remaining iteration budget.
+Persistence must retain that failure and recovery requirement across restarts.
+An upstream provider correction is separate work; this release does not claim
+to improve the model's probability output.
+
+### Operator workflow
+
+Proposed command contract, to be frozen in the first implementation PR:
 
 ```text
 dev-agent . "Fix the bug and add regression tests" --orchestrate --save-run
 dev-agent --list-runs
 dev-agent --show-run <run-id>
-dev-agent --resume <run-id>
+dev-agent --resume <run-id> [--plain]
 ```
 
-Saving is opt-in for orchestration. Listing and showing runs are read-only
-local operations with bounded output. `--resume` explicitly reopens a saved
-orchestration run; every resolved action still requires approval. Keep these
-options distinct from existing repository/task positional arguments, and keep
-decision-only behavior unchanged. Run IDs resolve only inside the application's
-run store; they are not arbitrary file paths or shell arguments.
-
-The first release supports continuation on the same machine and canonical
-repository/worktree after a typed stop, an evaluation-failure stop, or a signal
-interruption whose process cleanup completed. Finished runs and runs at the
-iteration limit remain inspectable. Resume cannot grant extra iterations or
-worker calls. A new task with a new budget is a separate explicit run.
-
-An unclean termination with an unresolved execution is inspectable but cannot
-resume execution in this first slice. Never replay an uncertain action, assume
-an orphaned worker has exited, or roll back partial edits. Cross-machine
-transfer, background workers, worker-native conversation restoration, and
-automatic retry after a crash are later scope.
-
-### Saved-run and continuation contract
-
-- Store a bounded, versioned checkpoint separately from JSONL traces. Current
-  traces truncate values and arrays and cannot reconstruct complete state;
-  neither old nor new traces become executable resume inputs. Freeze the
-  checkpoint's schema, size limits, status transitions, and compatibility rules
-  before integrating execution. Unsupported versions must fail explicitly.
-- Preserve the original task, bounded approved context and its provenance,
-  repository identity, instruction/validation metadata, frozen provider/model,
-  worker selection and network permission, consumed budgets, and failure
-  history. Keep transport objects, credentials, raw environment values,
-  AbortSignal, and executable approval objects out of the format. Record only
-  non-secret configuration identity; reload credentials from the operator's
-  environment and reject provider/account or permission changes during resume.
-- Use an operator-owned application state directory outside worker-writable
-  repositories, with restricted access, bounded reads, and atomic checkpoint
-  replacement. Define integrity and sequence checks against an authoritative
-  local attempt ledger. Validate persisted content as untrusted input; a
-  checksum by itself is not authorization. Reject malformed, truncated,
-  altered, or stale checkpoints instead of repairing counters or flags.
-- Record iteration consumption before evaluation and reserve worker allowance
-  durably before dispatch. Record outcomes without charging the same attempt
-  twice. An uncertain reserved attempt stays charged and is reported as
-  uncertain, without inventing a successful execution or an approval. If a
-  required durable write fails, start no further evaluation or execution;
-  drain any active cleanup and explain the last trustworthy checkpoint.
-- Acquire exclusive ownership of the saved run and prevent another app-managed
-  run from using the same worktree concurrently. An unresolved active owner or
-  stale lock blocks execution; never kill a process based only on a saved PID.
-  The design must account for process cleanup before a run becomes resumable.
-- Refresh repository state before continuation. A different worktree, changed
-  HEAD, unavailable repository, or unbounded/ambiguous identity check blocks
-  resume. Show any working-tree drift, retain historical evidence as historical,
-  and use the existing clarification/preparation gates when task context needs
-  review. Changed instruction files require new bounded reads and approval.
-  Do not restore Git state, replace files, or revert operator edits.
-- Start a fresh validation generation on resume; prior passing checks remain
-  history and cannot authorize completion. Rebuild candidates from current
-  state and require new approvals, including acceptance review for `FINISH`.
-  Resume of an evaluation failure retains its explicit recovery requirement.
-  A saved proposal, old approval, or worker test claim grants no authority.
-- Retain the eight-iteration and two-calls-per-adapter ceilings across every
-  process segment. Selection and permission flags remain immutable; fresh
-  validation also consumes the remaining budget. Insufficient budget must
-  produce the existing bounded stop rather than silently extend the run.
-  Link segment traces and summaries by run identity while keeping metrics
-  outside authorization state. Measure active time with each process's local
-  monotonic clock; time between sessions is not active work or prompt wait.
-
-### Implementation order
-
-1. [ ] Define the checkpoint schema, attempt ledger, storage bounds, and
-   lifecycle. Document exactly which fields are restored, revalidated, or
-   historical, and how integrity, write ordering, locks, and compatibility are
-   enforced. Add offline fixtures for clean stops, exhausted limits, incomplete
-   writes, altered counters/permissions, stale checkpoints, and unresolved
-   executions. No execution path may accept a saved record until this contract
-   is validated.
-2. [ ] Add opt-in persistence to the existing orchestration lifecycle. Persist
-   budget reservations before dispatch and completed transitions afterward;
-   preserve existing signal cleanup and trace behavior. Test failures before
-   and after each durable boundary so restarting cannot duplicate execution,
-   reset budgets, or lose an in-flight attempt from the record.
-3. [ ] Add local run listing and inspection with the plain and styled CLI
-   presentation. Show task/repository identity, last status, remaining budgets,
-   pending validation, failure/interruption, and a specific resume blocker.
-   These commands must not call a provider, invoke a worker, or change the
-   selected repository. Keep context bounded and credentials redacted.
-4. [ ] Add explicit resume for eligible saved runs. Resolve the same repository
-   and immutable configuration, obtain exclusive ownership, refresh evidence,
-   invalidate validation, and enter the loop at the next unconsumed iteration.
-   Retain approved clarification provenance and failure history; require the
-   existing action, recovery, and completion decisions. Incompatible or
-   incomplete records remain inspectable without being executable.
-5. [ ] Verify and prepare v0.6.0. Exercise stop/restart/resume through mocked
-   provider/process boundaries for both workers and all supported routes, plus
-   an operator-authorized live stop/resume walkthrough for each worker. Cover
-   cancellation, EOF, changed worktrees/instructions, missing credentials,
-   storage failures, concurrent resumes, and exhausted budgets. Run focused
-   tests, typecheck, the full suite, build, schema validation, and installed
-   package checks; document migration, local storage, and known limits. Record
-   release source and archive evidence, give advance npm authentication notice,
-   and verify publication through a separate registry installation.
-
-### Release gate
-
-- [ ] A cleanly stopped saved run resumes in a new CLI process, preserves task
-  context and remaining limits, and finishes only after fresh validation and
-  explicit acceptance approval. Both worker adapters are covered.
-- [ ] Old approvals, changed permissions, wrong repository identity, tampered
-  or incompatible state, unresolved attempts, and concurrent owners cannot
-  cause execution. Exhausted budgets cannot be reset through resume.
-- [ ] Failure-injection tests establish durable write ordering and conservative
-  attempt accounting. Trace compatibility, credential exclusion, cleanup, and
-  preservation of operator edits pass their regressions.
-- [ ] History and both presentation modes clearly distinguish resumable,
-  blocked, finished, and budget-exhausted runs. The exact installed package and
-  recorded live walkthroughs pass before release.
+Saving is opt-in and requires `--orchestrate`. The supported saved-run target
+is a Git worktree with a resolvable HEAD; ordinary unsaved operation keeps its
+existing repository support. The initial review explains what is stored and
+where. Stop, EOF, and signals retain their existing meaning and exit behavior;
+the terminal summary also prints the run ID and continuation status.
+
+Listing and showing are bounded, read-only local operations. A missing
+repository or missing provider credential must not prevent inspection. Plain
+output remains available; history JSON output is deferred so existing
+decision-only `--json` behavior stays stable. Run IDs resolve only within the
+application store and never accept arbitrary file paths.
+
+Resume uses the stored task and repository rather than new positional
+arguments. It shows the prior stop, remaining limits, refreshed repository
+changes, pending checks, and immutable selections before the operator chooses
+to continue or stop. That review grants no action approval. Resume rejects
+task, worker, network, mock/live, or provider/model overrides; presentation
+choice may change. Recovery from an evaluation failure remains explicit and
+does not get counted or requested twice by overlapping resume/recovery prompts.
+
+Example: three consumed evaluations and one Codex call leave five iterations
+and one Codex call. Resume starts at iteration four. Fresh validation consumes
+those remaining iterations; finishing is never promised when too little
+budget remains. Finished and exhausted runs stay inspectable.
+
+| Last condition | Proposed continuation behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Typed stop or EOF, with durable state and completed cleanup | Eligible after repository/configuration review. |
+| Evaluation failure stopped by the operator | Eligible with explicit recovery and budget remaining. |
+| SIGINT/SIGTERM, including during a worker, with recorded outcome and completed cleanup | Eligible after refresh; partial edits and charged attempts remain. |
+| Abrupt exit, unresolved attempt/owner, or incomplete required write | Blocked; show the last trustworthy evidence and uncertainty. |
+| Finished or iteration limit reached | Inspection only; resume cannot extend the run. |
+| Unknown schema, altered/stale record, wrong worktree, changed HEAD, or unverifiable identity | Blocked; never repair the record or relocate the task implicitly. |
+
+### State and durability requirements
+
+Use a dedicated versioned saved-run format, separate from diagnostic JSONL
+traces. The current traces deliberately truncate data; they cannot supply
+resume state. The first contract must classify each saved field:
+
+| Treatment | Data |
+| --- | --- |
+| Restore after strict validation | Original task; bounded approved clarification/issue context and provenance; failure history; consumed budgets and original ceiling; immutable provider/model, mock/live, worker selection, and network permission. |
+| Refresh or revalidate | Canonical repository/Git worktree identity and HEAD; working-tree changes; instruction fingerprints; validation scripts, coverage, and all original required checks. |
+| Retain only as history | Earlier test outcomes, worker summaries, proposals/approval receipts, interruptions, and segment metrics. |
+| Never persist | Credentials, raw environment values, transport instances, AbortSignal, raw rejected provider responses, or an executable approved candidate. |
+
+Required context must fit the schema without lossy truncation of acceptance
+criteria or validation requirements. Apply bounded, credential-aware text
+handling; if required context cannot be represented safely, stop saving and
+explain the blocker instead of silently making a resumable record. Opt-in
+storage can contain task text and source excerpts; document that local data
+and its retention without claiming encryption or perfect secret detection.
+
+The store belongs to the operator and must be outside worker-writable
+repositories. PR 1 must settle platform paths, restricted access, link/path
+rejection, explicit byte/event/record limits, atomic replacement, flush/write
+ordering, and schema compatibility. A checksum alone cannot make a checkpoint
+authoritative. Bind it to an integrity-checked, sequenced local attempt ledger
+and reject mismatched or older records. No schema migration or trace import is
+required for v0.6; incompatible records remain non-executable.
+
+State the trust boundary honestly: protecting records from repository text,
+restricted workers, corruption, and checkpoint-only rollback does not establish
+protection from a compromised operator account or rollback of the entire local
+store. The contract must explain which authority is protected and prove the
+claimed behavior on POSIX and Windows before persistence enters the loop.
+
+Consume an iteration durably before evaluation. After a fresh action approval,
+record the dispatch boundary before every tool/worker execution and reserve a
+worker allowance before starting that worker. Commit outcomes without charging
+twice. An uncertain reservation stays charged and blocks continuation; never
+invent an approval or replay an uncertain action. Required persistence or trace
+write failure stops further evaluation/execution and drains active cleanup.
+
+Acquire exclusive run ownership and a canonical-worktree lock. Every
+app-managed orchestration invocation, including an unsaved one, must respect
+an active saved-run owner of that worktree. A stale/unresolved owner blocks
+execution; a saved PID alone cannot authorize lock removal or process killing.
+Mark a stop resumable only after the action outcome, repository refresh, process
+cleanup, and final durable transition are known.
+
+Freeze non-secret configuration identity and reload credentials from the
+operator's environment. Explicit provider/model or Cloudflare account changes
+block continuation. The present configuration has no non-secret account ID for
+the other providers; PR 1 must decide and document credential-continuity rules
+before enabling resume. A variable name cannot prove account identity, and
+credential values must not be stored to fill that gap. Preserve the selected
+model identifier; a provider alias such as `jev-latest` does not guarantee the
+same underlying served version on a later day.
+
+### Continuation and policy requirements
+
+Reinspect the same canonical worktree and unchanged HEAD. Compare bounded
+working-tree fingerprints, including untracked changes relevant to the task;
+status filenames alone do not prove unchanged contents. Show drift for review,
+invalidate stale reads, and require new approved reads for changed instruction
+files. An unavailable or ambiguous comparison blocks continuation. Never reset
+Git, restore files, discard partial edits, or attribute operator edits to a
+worker. Retain exact linked-issue identity and clarification provenance; any
+new issue fetch still uses the existing approved read boundary.
+
+Start a fresh validation generation on resume. Keep original required checks,
+including those named by the task, issue, and clarifications; a removed script
+cannot silently remove its requirement. Prior passing checks and worker claims
+cannot establish completion. A prior failure cannot establish current-generation
+repair eligibility: rerun the relevant independent check before another repair
+when policy requires it. Rebuild every candidate from current state and obtain
+a new action approval, including acceptance review for `FINISH`.
+
+The original eight-iteration maximum, two calls per adapter, 95% automatic
+completion threshold, preparation gates, repeated-failure rules, and fixed
+worker/network selection span every process segment. Preserve a lower original
+iteration ceiling if one was used. Never reset or transfer budgets, redirect an
+excluded route, relax probability validation, or silently switch providers.
+
+Link each segment's traces and summaries to the saved-run ID. Preserve trace
+compatibility and keep reporting metrics outside AgentState and authorization.
+Use a fresh local monotonic clock per segment; time between processes is neither
+active work nor prompt wait. Show cumulative attempt counts from durable records
+without double-counting recovery rows or treating metrics as permission.
+
+### Six proposed implementation PRs
+
+Each PR has a reviewable result and focused tests. Add the contract and failure
+fixtures before wiring saved data into execution; use the current small typed
+modules rather than introducing a workflow framework.
+
+1. [ ] **Saved-run contract and storage foundation.** Define schema version 1,
+   field bounds, lifecycle/stop reasons, ledger ordering, repository identity,
+   configuration/credential continuity, integrity, and ownership. Implement the
+   bounded store and offline fixtures without an executable resume route.
+   Demonstrate clean read/write, malformed/incompatible input rejection,
+   altered counters/permissions, stale snapshots, partial writes, and lock
+   contention. Record POSIX/Windows guarantees and limits. This is the next
+   implementation task; unresolved durability or identity decisions block PR 2.
+2. [ ] **Opt-in saving throughout the loop.** Add `--save-run`, create the run
+   before its first evaluation, and persist reservations and outcomes at the
+   established boundaries. Preserve signal cleanup, prompts, trace writes,
+   unsaved behavior, and exit codes. Print the saved ID/status. Inject failures
+   before and after evaluation, approval, dispatch, outcome, and clean stop;
+   assert no unrecorded execution, double charge, or false resumable status.
+3. [ ] **Local run history.** Add `--list-runs` and `--show-run` with bounded
+   listing and a way to inspect an older known ID. Display status, task/repo,
+   budgets, selections, pending validation, last failure, and precise blockers.
+   Cover empty/corrupt stores, unavailable repositories, terminal sanitization,
+   and plain/styled output. Prove these commands work without credentials,
+   provider calls, worker launches, or repository mutations.
+4. [ ] **Explicit resume.** Add CLI compatibility checks, exclusive ownership,
+   preflight/review, fresh evaluator binding, repository/context refresh,
+   validation invalidation, and entry at the next unused iteration. Add a
+   two-process happy path for each worker selection and explicit recovery
+   continuation. Prove old approvals never execute, budgets span restarts, and
+   all current policy/candidate/final-approval guards still apply.
+5. [ ] **Restart and platform verification.** Extend deterministic integration
+   coverage across all six supported evaluation routes and both workers.
+   Exercise repeated restarts, exhausted budgets, missing/conflicting config,
+   changed HEAD/worktree/content/instructions/scripts, concurrent owners,
+   storage errors, EOF, signals, and unresolved execution. Extend the compiled
+   and installed PTY/Windows ConPTY matrix on supported Node versions. Keep
+   existing decision-only, unsaved orchestration, and JSON behavior covered.
+6. [ ] **Live pilot and v0.6.0 release.** Freeze a candidate archive and bounded
+   protocol, obtain operator authorization for live calls, then run the pilot
+   below before any publication. Fix failures in a separately identified
+   candidate with retained observations. Record package/source provenance,
+   migration/storage guidance, limitations, and release acceptance. Give
+   advance npm authentication notice before timed login/publication; verify
+   the published archive and a fresh registry installation afterward.
+
+### Verification and release acceptance
+
+The live pilot is a release requirement, planned from the outset. It uses the
+exact installed candidate, actual default TypeSafe/Jev evaluation, and actual
+workers with separate action approvals. Freeze tasks, fixtures, stop points,
+maximum launches/time/spend, acceptance oracles, and candidate/tool versions
+before calls. Planning this pilot does not authorize spending or publication.
+

+# Saved-run storage contract v1
+
+This document records the storage contract introduced for v0.6 PR 1. It is a
+local persistence foundation only: the CLI does not create, list, show, or
+resume saved runs yet. Saved records are never executable instructions or
+approved candidates.
+
+## Files and bounds
+
+The default store is outside the repository:
+
+- Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\dev-orchestrator\\saved-runs`, falling back to
+  `%USERPROFILE%\\AppData\\Local\\dev-orchestrator\\saved-runs`.
+- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/dev-orchestrator/saved-runs`.
+- Other Unix systems: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/dev-orchestrator/saved-runs`, falling
+  back to `~/.local/state/dev-orchestrator/saved-runs`.
+
+The store contains `runs/<uuid>/checkpoint.json`,
+`runs/<uuid>/events.jsonl`, and ownership files under `locks/`. It is rejected
+when located inside the selected worker-writable repository. Run IDs are
+version-4 UUIDs; callers cannot choose a path through an ID.
+
+| Record | Limit |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Checkpoint | 1 MiB |
+| Event record | 4 KiB |
+| Events per run | 128 |
+| Runs per store | 128 |
+| Orchestration iteration ceiling | 8 |
+| Calls per worker | 2 |
+
+The v1 checkpoint has exactly these top-level fields: `schemaVersion`,
+`runId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `sequence`, `ledgerHead`, `status`,
+`iterationLimit`, `repository`, `configuration`, `state`, and `checksum`.
+The repository identity contains the canonical worktree root, Git common
+directory, full HEAD object ID, and a worktree fingerprint. Configuration
+freezes mock/live mode, provider and model identifiers, worker selection, and
+Codex network permission. Cloudflare records also contain a SHA-256 fingerprint
+of the account ID; the account ID itself is not stored.
+
+`state` is a bounded, validated `AgentState`. Known current environment
+credentials are redacted from persisted text. Provider keys, Cloudflare account
+IDs, raw environment values, transport objects, abort signals, raw provider
+responses, and executable candidates are excluded. Task text and bounded
+repository excerpts can still contain sensitive information; the local store
+is not encrypted, and pattern-based redaction cannot identify every secret.
+
+## Event ledger and ordering
+
+Events use schema version 1 and are stored as one JSON object per newline. Each
+event contains a sequence number, timestamp, previous-event hash, immutable run
+identity hash, resulting state hash, event data, and SHA-256 event hash. The
+checkpoint stores the current sequence and ledger head. Reads reject duplicate
+JSON keys, unknown versions, malformed or oversized records, sequence gaps,
+hash mismatches, identity changes, and checkpoint/ledger disagreement. No
+migration or trace import is defined; unknown versions are inspection failures
+and must never be resumed.
+
+The event vocabulary records run creation and continuation, iteration
+reservations, completed/failed evaluations, explicit action approvals,
+execution reservations and outcomes, clarifications, clean stops, completion,
+iteration exhaustion, and blocked states. Validation enforces increasing
+iterations, the original ceiling, worker-call limits, exact call-counter
+agreement, approval before dispatch, matching execution outcomes, and current
+independent validation plus a fresh `FINISH` approval before a finished status.
+Stops and continuations discard any outstanding action approval. An unresolved
+execution prevents a resumable stop. These checks validate stored history; they
+do not replace the orchestration policy or independently establish that task
+acceptance criteria were met.
+
+## Durability and ownership
+
+On POSIX, the store and run directories use mode `0700`, and record and lock
+files use `0600`. Writes use a private temporary file, file flush, atomic rename,
+and directory flush where supported. Event appends flush the file and parent
+directory. A failure between the ledger append and checkpoint replacement can
+leave a mismatch; the store rejects that record instead of guessing which
+state is current. The store rejects symbolic links and hard-linked record
+files. It does not clean up stale locks automatically; an existing owner file
+blocks another owner because a PID is not proof that a lock is safe to remove.
+
+On Windows, the implementation requests restrictive creation modes, but
+effective access control is inherited from the parent directory and is not
+verified or rewritten as an ACL. Directory flushing is skipped because Node's
+portable filesystem API does not provide the same supported operation there.
+The Windows-specific filesystem and terminal matrix remains part of the later
+v0.6 verification milestone; this PR's automated storage tests ran on POSIX.
+
+Exclusive lock files coordinate processes using this store. A run lock keys one
+run; a worktree lock keys its canonical root. Lock files are created with
+exclusive-create semantics and removed only by their recorded token owner.
+External editors and older CLI versions do not participate in these locks.
+
+SHA-256 checks detect corruption and checkpoint-only edits or rollback when
+compared with the event ledger. They do not authenticate the operator, protect
+against a compromised local account, or detect a coordinated rewrite or
+rollback of the entire store. The saved directory must therefore remain under
+the operator's control and outside worker-writable repositories.
+
+## Credential continuity decision
+
+Resume will freeze the provider and model identifier and reload the selected
+credential from the operator's current environment. It will never save a
+credential value or compare a hash of one. Cloudflare's non-secret account ID
+can be compared using its stored fingerprint. The other configured providers
+expose no non-secret account identity in this client, so continuity for those
+credentials cannot be verified. Before implementing resume, its review must
+state that limitation and require an explicit operator continuation decision;
+reloading a credential does not prove that it belongs to the same account.
+
+Provider aliases such as `jev-latest` also do not pin the model implementation
+served later. The current schema binds the selected identifier, not a remote
+provider deployment or model revision.
*** End Patch";

+## Enforcement coverage
+
+`src/saved-runs/matrix.test.ts` exercises all six evaluator routes with both
+worker selections: direct TypeSafe/Jev, Vercel/Jev, OpenRouter/Jev,
+OpenRouter/OpenAI Decisions, and Cloudflare Clef/Clef-flash. Each of the 12
+combinations has a successful three-segment task and an exhausted-budget task,
+for 24 cases. Each segment binds a fresh evaluator using stored configuration
+and reconstructed durable state. HTTP and coding-worker boundaries are
+synthetic; Git inspection, policy, candidates, approval, execution transitions,
+independent Node checks, snapshots, and the store remain real.
+
+Successful tasks stop after implementation, resume to reread instructions and
+stop again, then resume to reread and independently validate before explicit
+completion acceptance. Seven distinct iteration reservations, one actual
+worker dispatch, three trace segments, and fresh validation generation 3 are
+asserted. A moderate completion assessment requires selecting FINISH and then
+approving its resolved candidate. Previous approvals never execute again.
+
+Exhaustion tasks consume both calls to the selected worker over separate
+segments, retain the excluded worker restriction, and stop at the original
+seven-iteration ceiling. Neither the model nor a manual alternative can grant
+a third call, transfer allowances, or finish without validation. The terminal
+result is `iteration_limit`, exit 1, with the patch and ledger preserved.
+
+CLI failure checks block before evaluator binding, review, approval, or dispatch
+for missing credentials, conflicting/empty selectors, changed Cloudflare
+account, changed HEAD, unavailable repositories or instructions, run/worktree
+owners, invalid snapshots, partial ledgers, and unresolved execution. Removed
+validation scripts remain required after content review. Existing store and
+loop fixtures additionally exercise partial writes, failed persistence at each
+boundary, stale ownership, unknown schemas, cancellation, and explicit
+evaluation recovery. These tests use deterministic fixtures without live calls.

+
+The [optional harness](../scripts/terminal/README.md) retains the 33 original
+unsaved terminal scenarios and adds 14 saved-run scenarios, for 47 per full
+matrix. Each worker uses three separate CLI processes for its accepted task;
+additional processes stop at the continuation review with typed stop, EOF,
+Ctrl+C, and timeout. Styled Codex enables networking explicitly; plain Claude
+retains restricted tools. Empty/invalid review input grants nothing. Declined
+reviews leave checkpoint and ledger bytes unchanged and release ownership.
+
+Each walkthrough also checks six preflight blockers per worker in bounded pipe
+processes, plus credential-free list/show. After the second clean stop, the
+harness changes instruction and check contents. The final review displays
+these changes, rereads instructions, performs independent validation, and
+requires a separate completion approval. Actual worker launch counts, durable
+iterations, validation generations, trace linkage, and empty ownership
+directories are asserted. State homes are isolated outside worker repositories
+on each platform; real operator history and credentials are never loaded.

+and credential redaction, raw mode/cursor/signal cleanup, POSIX terminal flags,
+prompt and active-process interruption, partial edits, current-generation
